- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. - iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.

Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". 137	-## Goal
138	-
139	-Turn the Python `hsim` driver into a single compiled C++20 executable named
140	-**`andesim`** that is a *framework* hosting multiple simulator backends behind
141	-one clear, self-describing interface - so QEMU (fast), Verilator (accurate),
142	-Hybrid, and future simulators (alioth, sid) are all first-class, and new

145	-## Vocabulary (three orthogonal concepts)
146	-
147	-- **Engine** = one simulator *process* the framework drives: `qemu`,
148	-  `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`, `verilator:ax66_makatau`, later `alioth`, `sid`.
149	-  This is the *pluggable* unit. Verilator has many engine instances (one per HW
150	-  config); QEMU has one.
151	-- **Model** = how chosen engines compose for a run:
152	-  - `fast`     = QEMU alone (functional).
153	-  - `accurate` = one Verilator alone, **pure - from reset, no QEMU** (cycle-accurate).
154	-  - `hybrid`   = QEMU fast-forward -> Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
155	-- **Trigger** = the ROI delimiter, used by `hybrid`: `marker` | `pc`.
156	-
157	-A run is `(model) x (engine) x (trigger)`.

159	-## Locked decisions
160	-
161	-- **Name:** the binary is `andesim` (the `hsim` "hybrid-sim" name retires).
162	-- **Language: C++20**, existing clang++ toolchain; `#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"`
163	-  directly (no hand-copied struct, no offsets).
164	-- **Runtime = pure C++** (no Python, no shell on the run path). **Build and test
165	-  infrastructure may stay shell/Python.**
166	-- **Plugins are drop-in binaries, not linked libraries.** Engines are external
167	-  processes; `andesim` is never recompiled to add one. No `dlopen`, no
168	-  compiled-in engine list.
169	-- **Discovery = scan + `--describe`.** The framework scans an engines directory
170	-  and asks each binary to self-report its capabilities as JSON. A sidecar
171	-  `<bin>.json` is the fallback for binaries that cannot add the flag. This is the
172	-  hot-plug query mechanism.
173	-- **Transparent passthrough for `fast`/`accurate`.** The framework parses only its
174	-  selection flags; everything after `--` forwards verbatim to the engine. In these
175	-  modes it inherits stdin/stdout/stderr, applies **no timeout**, and propagates the
176	-  engine's exit code (exec-style). All native engine behavior is preserved - e.g.
177	-  QEMU can hold a gdbstub and wait for a debugger. Users experience one simulator.
178	-- **`accurate` = pure Verilator from reset, no QEMU.** vsim already supports this
179	-  (default path; hybrid is gated by `--resume-from-qemu`). Cycles come from vsim's
180	-  own output, not a drained state file.
181	-- **No QEMU2 handback.** No gdbstub state-restore into a second QEMU. The `hybrid`
182	-  cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta. The QEMU2 leg was removed from the repo
183	-  entirely (`tests/e2e.sh` is a 2-phase harness now).

185	-## Architecture (three layers)
186	-
187	-```
188	- andesim  (one C++20 binary; libc++ + include/hybrid/state_abi.h only)
189	-   |
190	- [1] ENGINE REGISTRY  -- discover at runtime (the hot-plug seam)
191	-   |     scan engines dir -> run `<bin> --describe` -> EngineDescriptor (JSON)
192	-   |     qemu (built-in descriptor) | verilator:<cfg> (self-describe) | alioth/sid (self-describe)
193	-   |
194	- [2] MODEL = composition  -- how chosen engines combine
195	-   |     fast      = [ qemu ]                      transparent passthrough
196	-   |     accurate  = [ verilator:<cfg> ]           transparent passthrough (from reset)
197	-   |     hybrid    = [ qemu --ff--> verilator ]    orchestrated, + trigger
198	-   |

200	-         run_plan(steps): per step -> registry invoke template -> spawn+timeout -> drain

206	-## Engine interface (the contract alioth/sid follow)
207	-
208	-A simulator joins the framework by doing two things:
209	-
210	-**1. Self-describe.** Answer `--describe` with one JSON object:
211	-
212	-```json
213	-{
214	-  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
215	-  "type":     "verilator",            // qemu | verilator | alioth | sid | ...
216	-  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",       // functional | cycle-accurate
217	-  "vlen":     512, "xlen": 64,        // optional HW params
218	-  "triggers": ["marker","pc"],  // ROI delimiters understood
219	-  "roles":    ["standalone","accurate-leg"],  // standalone | fast-leg | accurate-leg
220	-  "state":    ["resume","drain"],     // hybrid_state_v1 capabilities (omit if none)
221	-  "invoke": {                         // argv prefix per role; {placeholders} filled by the framework

225	-  },
